record.paper_title: Some open problems and research directions in the mathematical study of fluid dynamics.
record.original_question: For three-dimensional Navier-Stokes flow past a bounded simply connected obstacle B, in the exterior domain Ω = R^3 minus B with velocity tending to a nonzero constant vector U at spatial infinity, can one prove realistic upper bounds for the bulk energy dissipation rate?

evidence.quote: A specific open problem remains: to provide realistic upper bounds for the dissipation

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a bounded simply connected domain (an obstacle) with smooth boundary, and let $\Omega = \mathbb{R}^3 \setminus \overline{B}$ be the exterior domain. Consider the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations
$$\partial_t u + (u\cdot\nabla)u = -\nabla p + \nu \Delta u, \qquad \nabla\cdot u = 0 \quad \text{in } \Omega,$$
with kinematic viscosity $\nu>0$, no-slip boundary condition $u=0$ on $\partial B$, and prescribed uniform flow at infinity
$$u(x,t) \to U \quad \text{as } |x|\to\infty,$$
for some fixed nonzero constant vector $U \in \mathbb{R}^3$. Define the bulk energy dissipation rate
$$\varepsilon = \limsup_{T\to\infty}\frac{1}{T}\int_0^T \frac{\nu}{|B|}\int_\Omega |\nabla u(x,t)|^2\,dx\,dt$$
(or, equivalently, the time-averaged drag power per unit obstacle volume).

Problem: Establish rigorous, physically realistic upper bounds for $\varepsilon$ in terms of $|U|$, $\nu$, and the geometry of $B$ (e.g. of the form $\varepsilon \le C\, |U|^3/L$ for a characteristic length $L$ of $B$ and a constant $C$ depending only on the shape of $B$), directly from the Navier–Stokes equations without ad hoc closure assumptions.
artifact.status_search_result: Rigorous bulk dissipation upper bounds (à la Doering–Constantin/Howard) have been established in several settings—body-forced turbulence, shear flows, Kolmogorov forcing—but obtaining realistic upper bounds for the bulk energy dissipation rate for 3D Navier–Stokes flow past a bounded obstacle in an exterior domain with nonzero velocity at infinity remains an open problem; the search did not return a rigorous proof of such bounds in this exterior-flow setting.

status_evidence.title: Bounds on dissipation for Navier–Stokes flow with Kolmogorov forcing
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds on the bulk rate of energy dissipation are derived for Kolmogorov-forced flows.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous dissipation bounds exist for forced (periodic) Navier–Stokes flows, not for exterior obstacle flow.

status_evidence.title: Energy dissipation in body-forced turbulence
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds on the bulk rate of energy dissipation in body-force-driven steady-state turbulence are derived directly from the Navier–Stokes equations.
status_evidence.claim: Analogous bounds are known for body-forced turbulence but the obstacle/exterior-domain analogue is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Stationary Solutions to the Navier–Stokes System in an Exterior Plane Domain
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of long-standing open problems for stationary Navier–Stokes flow in exterior domains.
status_evidence.claim: Exterior-domain stationary Navier–Stokes problems remain a source of open questions.
